name: Creality Falcon T1 20W Fiber
tagline: 20W fiber galvo module for stainless and aluminum on the T1 chassis
tldr: Creality's 20W fiber WaveSync module turns the Falcon T1 into a metal-marking galvo without buying a separate fiber bench. Ideal when steel and aluminum orders justify the module cost after you already own the T1 cabinet.
mainObjective: Desktop fiber marking on the modular T1 platform

priceRange.note: Official Creality store, Oct 2026: $2,699, complete machine

engraveExample.description: Filled logo on stainless steel plate

cannot: Use alongside diode module without swapping

pros: Bare-metal marking without a separate fiber machine
Very fine spot (about 0.02 mm) for serial numbers and small text
Lowest-priced metal module for the T1 ($1,099 alone, October 2026)
cons: No cutting of wood, leather or acrylic
No colour marking on stainless: that needs a MOPA source with pulse control
Coated metals and marking sprays still need fume extraction
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 20W SKU on Creality Falcon T1 Fiber. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other modules via the chips before buying.
proTips: Keep separate material libraries for fiber vs diode heads. Confirm EZCAD/LightBurn support on your exact module SKU before buying.
primaryUse: 20W fiber galvo module for metal marking on the Creality Falcon T1 modular workstation.

moduleSystem.headline: WaveSync swappable galvo modules
moduleSystem.description: One enclosed T1 chassis accepts Creality diode (20W/40W), fiber (20W), MOPA (60W), and UV (5W) modules: install one head at a time.

editorialDepth.advantages: Creality Falcon T1 Fiber 20W fits shops that mark stainless, aluminum, and tools daily without a CO₂ bay. A solid bench option for jewelry, tags, and small batches.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if wood, leather, or cast acrylic pay your bills. Deep metal cutting and large industrial panels often need more fiber headroom (40W or 60W) or a different machine class.

faq.question: What does the T1 fiber module do that the diode cannot?
faq.answer: It marks and engraves bare metals (stainless steel, aluminium, brass) and some hard plastics, with a spot of about 0.02 mm. A filled 10 × 10 cm logo on stainless took about 2–5 min in our benchmark. It does not cut wood, leather or acrylic.

faq.question: How much is the T1 with the fiber module?
faq.answer: On Creality's US store in October 2026 the T1 with the 20W fiber module was $2,699, and the fiber module alone was $1,099 for owners of another T1 bundle. Prices move with promotions, so check the store on the day.

faq.question: 20W fiber or 60W MOPA on the T1?
faq.answer: The 20W fiber covers logos, serial numbers and light engraving on metal. The 60W MOPA ($4,299 bundle, $1,600 more) adds pulse control for colour marking on stainless and is quicker for deep engraving. Take the fiber unless colour or deep engraving is billable work.

standoutFeatures.title: Metal marking in the T1 enclosure
standoutFeatures.body: The fiber module turns the T1 into a metal marker for stainless, aluminium and brass, without a second machine on the bench.

standoutFeatures.title: Very fine spot
standoutFeatures.body: With a spot of about 0.02 mm, QR codes, serial numbers and small logos stay sharp on tags and tools.
